wy-spi-2026-harshman-steve.name: Steve Harshman
wy-spi-2026-harshman-steve.bio: Longtime Wyoming teacher and coach at Natrona County High School and former Wyoming legislator.

positions.stance: Focus is to "support students, honor the full education team, strengthen reading and career readiness," and help Wyoming kids build futures at home.
Believes "strong families, respected teachers, local school boards, and practical Wyoming solutions are what keep schools strong."

ca-spi-2026-barrera-richard.name: Richard Barrera
ca-spi-2026-barrera-richard.bio: President of the San Diego Unified School Board, to which he was first elected in 2008.

positions.stance: Supports helping districts fund and build workforce housing for teachers and staff and expanding statewide programs for educators struggling with housing costs.
Calls for a statewide effort to increase education funding, hold the federal government to its special-education obligations, and help districts pass local funding measures.
Supports "free, universal, high-quality early childhood education for every three-year-old in California" with fair pay for early educators.
Supports paid teacher apprenticeships, covering tuition for those who commit to teaching in California public schools, and fair pay for current teachers.
Supports protecting LGBTQ+ students' rights, responding to bullying, expanding dual-language immersion, and offering vocational and career pathways.

ca-spi-2026-shaw-sonja.name: Sonja Shaw
ca-spi-2026-shaw-sonja.bio: President of the Chino Valley Unified School Board, elected in 2022.

positions.stance: Opposes policies allowing "boys to undress in girls' locker rooms and play on their sports teams," citing fairness, safety and parental consent.
Calls for a back-to-basics focus on reading, writing and math, plus recruiting and retaining top educators.
Says pandemic closures and mask and vaccine mandates silenced parents; "Parents must have a say" in education decisions.

tx-comptroller-2026-faizi-shehla.name: Shehla Faizi
tx-comptroller-2026-faizi-shehla.bio: Graphic design graduate with a career in advertising and marketing journalism.

positions.stance: Would seek legal opinions and support for the Comptroller's office to "divest from all foreign bonds," including Israel bonds.
Opposes tax breaks for data centers, saying the money is better spent on disaster relief and public schools.
Would seek legal opinions and political support "to end the unconstitutional anti-BDS law" administered by the Comptroller's office.
Would seek to dismantle "Divestment Statute Lists," make cost the top contracting factor, and administer school vouchers without religious bias.
Would challenge the legality and wisdom of SB8 grants rewarding sheriffs' cooperation with ICE; says sheriffs "must remain independent."

tx-agriculture-2026-kelly-austin.name: Austin R. Kelly
tx-agriculture-2026-kelly-austin.bio: Ecologist with a Ph.D. and founder of ARK Ecological Consulting.

positions.stance: Would cut red tape around hemp, cottage food and local meat processing and end "pay-to-play licensing schemes."
Opposes warrantless TDA inspections and eminent domain "for private gain or state convenience," and supports stronger right-to-farm protections.
Would launch "a full, forensic audit of the TDA on Day 1" and pass cost savings back to farmers as lower fees.
Says the state oversimplifies brush control as a water fix; would publish a transparent review of existing research for landowners.
Would shift funding from marketing to biosecurity monitoring, border prevention and early detection of invasive species and diseases.
"Let the market—not the government—decide the energy mix," with no subsidies or mandates for any energy source.
Would protect mineral and surface owners from "government overreach and eminent domain abuse" and favor voluntary, market-based dispute resolution.
Would hold operators accountable for well plugging and cleanup, using bonding and insurance markets instead of taxpayer bailouts.

mi-sos-2026-sloan-christine.name: Christine Sloan
mi-sos-2026-sloan-christine.bio: Has worked in health care for over a decade.

positions.stance: "Elected officials should answer to you — not to party bosses"; pledges to hold herself to the transparency standard she demands of others.
Believes government's role is narrow: protect individual rights, maintain essential services, and enforce fair and consistent laws.
Would "restrict government use of mass surveillance technology" such as Flock cameras and hold data collectors accountable.
Will push for open records, public budget hearings and plain-language reporting on how taxpayer dollars are used.
Criticizes debates "bought and paid for by large media corporations" in place of nonpartisan debates sponsored by the League of Women Voters.
Supports ranked choice voting in Michigan so voters can rank candidates instead of choosing "the lesser of two evils."
Would like to see the voting age lowered to 16 to give young people "some real power over their future."

mi-ag-2026-dye-jason.name: Jason Dye
mi-ag-2026-dye-jason.bio: Constitutional advocate and founder of WTPN.news.

positions.stance: Would create a public corruption task force targeting "government abuse, retaliation, fraud, coverups, and misuse of public office."
Would investigate patterns of misconduct, undisclosed conflicts and procedural weaponization in Michigan courtrooms.
Supports ending qualified immunity so people can hold government actors accountable when rights are violated.
Supports ending civil asset forfeiture: "No property taken without real due process, real evidence, and real accountability."
Would expose "backroom deals, NDA development agreements, hidden contracts, and public-records games."

ma-aud-2026-ozonoff-al.name: Al Ozonoff
ma-aud-2026-ozonoff-al.bio: Researcher and data-systems expert with more than twenty years working with complex information, programs and organizations.

positions.stance: Would examine major contracts, emergency procurement, vendor performance and cost changes, and "whether taxpayers received what was purchased."
Would use data analysis to identify improper or duplicate payments and check whether overpayments are recovered.
Would examine major public projects, including MBTA projects, for contract changes, schedule performance and lifecycle costs.
Would audit major state technology investments, including whether agencies have appropriate controls and safeguards.
Would examine licensing timelines, administrative delays, internal controls, enforcement consistency and fee administration.

in-sos-2026-shillings-lauri.name: Lauri A. Shillings
in-sos-2026-shillings-lauri.bio: Creative Director at the University of Indianapolis and small business owner since 2000.

positions.stance: Will run elections with clear rules and transparent processes and says voters' registration information "belongs to you."
Would fix the office's business registration system so filings are "fast, reliable, and intuitive."
Will expand plain-language voter education on registering, where to vote, ballot contents and absentee ballots.

in-sos-2026-ballard-greg.name: Greg Ballard
in-sos-2026-ballard-greg.bio: Former two-term mayor of Indianapolis and 23-year Marine veteran.

positions.stance: Would create Indiana's first statewide voter guide explaining each office and providing neutral candidate information and a sample ballot.
Would expand the recount commission to five members, all retired judges, so no single party appoints a majority.
Says Indiana should encourage more choices and competition; an independent's vote share can unlock ballot access for others.
Would establish hands-on training for county clerks and fund standardized poll worker training already authorized by law.
Supports a law barring a sitting Secretary of State from endorsing candidates, fundraising for parties, or holding party leadership roles.

mo-auditor-2026-coffell-dustin.name: Dustin Coffell
mo-auditor-2026-coffell-dustin.bio: Accountant with a master's degree in accounting and a background in corporate finance and financial analysis.

positions.stance: "No party should write its own report card"; promises fair, objective audits of agencies, counties and municipalities.
Would modernize state and local audits to include rigorous cybersecurity and data privacy standards.
Would audit agencies "budget line by budget line" to halt structural deficits and eliminate waste before reserves run out.

wi-sos-2026-karas-pete.name: Pete Karas
wi-sos-2026-karas-pete.bio: Small business owner and former Racine City Council member.

positions.stance: Calls the two-party system "fundamentally anti-democratic" and is running to give voters a meaningful third-party alternative.
Would gladly serve as chair of the Board of Commissioners of Public Lands, which funds public school libraries.
Supports "prioritizing school districts with the greatest needs" instead of equal per-student library funding.
Would expand digitization of historical records and create a searchable, accessible online records system.
Voting "should be a straightforward process with rigorous checks involved to prevent fraud."
It should be "easy and affordable for every Coloradan to establish and maintain their business."

co-sos-2026-campbell-amanda.name: Amanda Campbell
co-sos-2026-campbell-amanda.bio: Business woman and past business owner.

positions.stance: National and state constitutions "are laws which must be followed, even when politicians find them inconvenient."
"Voters have the right to set the rules for politicians, not the other way around."
Voters have the right to initiate controls on government "without fear of politicians' self-serving and arrogant interference."
Says the Secretary of State should defend the constitutions, warn legislators about unconstitutional bills, and even sue over unconstitutional laws.
"The process for businesses to work with and file information with the State needs to be updated and streamlined."
Opposes Colorado laws barring voters in the "wrong" political party from voting in special odd-year vacancy elections.
Supports letting 17-year-olds who will be 18 by the general election vote in primary elections.
Supports proportional voting methods to elect multi-member bodies, saying they make gerrymandering "virtually impossible."
Supports Approval Voting, ranked voting methods and STAR Voting for single-winner offices such as Secretary of State.
"A strong supporter of paper ballots"; would limit electronic ballot return and supports robust audits of counts and chain of custody.
